knowledge:
- key_parameters: snps=guidance on providing a SNP info file to read.pedfile ;; select.snps=numeric vector or names to select a subset of SNPs during PLINK import ;; fields=named vector mapping columns (snp, sample, genotype, confidence, allele.A, allele.B) to read long-format files ;; threshold=confidence threshold for calling genotypes in read.long ;; pairwise=logical indicating whether to calculate pairwise Fst between strata or overall ;; stats=character vector specifying LD statistics to calculate (e.g., "D.prime", "R.squared", "OR") ;; depth=maximum distance (in SNPs) between pairs of SNPs to calculate LD ;; rules=imputation rules object generated by snp.imputation ;; uncertain=logical indicating whether to use posterior probabilities for uncertain genotypes in single.snp.tests
- alternatives: read.mach can be used to read imputation outputs from MACH1 instead of generating rules via snp.imputation
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing genome-wide association study (GWAS) data, calculating LD matrices, performing genotype imputation from a reference panel, or running association tests (single-SNP or right-hand side regression) on observed or imputed genotypes.
- pitfalls: Failing to set an appropriate threshold in read.long can lead to low-quality genotype calls being included. Imputation rules must be generated using matching physical positions (pos.pres and pos.miss) to ensure correct mapping. When pooling scores with pool(), ensure score=TRUE was set in the preceding single.snp.tests calls.

workflows.name: data_input
workflows.intent: Load SNP genotype data from PED/INFO, PLINK, or long-format text files into SnpMatrix objects.
workflows.stages: 1. Read PED/INFO files using read.pedfile ;; 2. Read PLINK files using read.plink ;; 3. Read long-format files using read.long
workflows.code:
pedfile <- system.file("extdata/sample.ped.gz", package="snpStats")
infofile <- system.file("extdata/sample.info", package="snpStats")
sample <- read.pedfile(pedfile, snps=infofile)
fam <- system.file("extdata/sample.fam", package="snpStats")
bim <- system.file("extdata/sample.bim", package="snpStats")
bed <- system.file("extdata/sample.bed", package="snpStats")
sample <- read.plink(bed, bim, fam)
subset <- read.plink(bed, bim, fam, select.snps=6:10)
longfile <- system.file("extdata/sample-long.gz", package="snpStats")
gdata <- read.long(longfile, fields=c(snp=1, sample=2, genotype=3, confidence=4), gcodes=c("1", "2", "3"), threshold=0.95)
allelesfile <- system.file("extdata/sample-long-alleles.gz", package="snpStats")
gdata <- read.long(allelesfile, fields=c(snp=1, sample=2, allele.A=3, allele.B=4, confidence=5), threshold=0.95)

workflows.name: ld_analysis
workflows.intent: Calculate and visualize linkage disequilibrium (LD) statistics between SNPs.
workflows.stages: 1. Calculate LD statistics using ld ;; 2. Plot LD matrix using image ;; 3. Calculate physical distance between SNPs using bandSparse ;; 4. Plot LD statistics against physical distance using hexbin ;; 5. Perform hierarchical clustering on LD-derived distances using hclust
workflows.code:
data(ld.example)
ld.ceph <- ld(ceph.1mb, stats=c("D.prime", "R.squared"), depth=100)
print(image(ld.ceph$D.prime, lwd=0))
spectrum <- rainbow(10, start=0, end=1/6)[10:1]
print(image(ld.ceph$D.prime, lwd=0, cuts=9, col.regions=spectrum, colorkey=TRUE))
pos <- support.ld$Position
diags <- vector("list", 100)
for (i in 1:100) diags[[i]] <- pos[(i+1):603] - pos[1:(603-i)]
dist <- bandSparse(603, k=1:100, diagonals=diags)
distance <- dist@x
D.prime <- ld.ceph$D.prime@x
R.squared <- ld.ceph$R.squared@x
plot(hexbin(D.prime^2, R.squared))
OR <- ld(ceph.1mb[,1], ceph.1mb[,5], stats="OR")
use <- pos>=1.579e7 & pos<=1.587e7
r2 <- forceSymmetric(ld.ceph$R.squared[use, use])
D <- as.dist(1-r2)
hc <- hclust(D, method="complete")
plot(hc)
clusters <- cutree(hc, h=0.5)

workflows.name: imputation_and_association
workflows.intent: Impute missing genotypes using a reference panel and perform association testing on imputed or pooled data.
input: subject.support (data frame containing phenotype and stratum data)
workflows.stages: 1. Generate imputation rules using snp.imputation ;; 2. Perform single-SNP association tests on imputed data using single.snp.tests ;; 3. Perform right-hand side regression tests using snp.rhs.tests ;; 4. Impute genotypes using impute.snps and plot uncertainty using plotUncertainty ;; 5. Pool association test scores using pool ;; 6. Switch alleles using switch.alleles
workflows.code:
data(for.exercise)
training <- sample(1000, 200)
select <- seq(1, ncol(snps.10),2) 
missing <- snps.10[training, select]
present <- snps.10[training, -select] 
target <- snps.10[-training, -select]
lost <- snps.10[-training, select]
pos.miss <- snp.support$position[select]
pos.pres <- snp.support$position[-select]
rules <- snp.imputation(present, missing, pos.pres, pos.miss)
summary(rules)
plot(rules)
imp <- single.snp.tests(cc, stratum, data=subject.support, snp.data=target, rules=rules)
obs <- single.snp.tests(cc, stratum, data=subject.support, snp.data=lost)
logP.imp <- -log10(p.value(imp, df=1))
logP.obs <- -log10(p.value(obs, df=1))
use <- imputation.r2(rules)>0.9
imp2 <- snp.rhs.tests(cc~strata(stratum), family="binomial", data=subject.support, snp.data=target, rules=rules)
imputed <- impute.snps(rules, target, as.numeric=FALSE)
plotUncertainty(imputed[, "rs4880568"])
imp3 <- single.snp.tests(cc, stratum, data=subject.support, snp.data=imputed, uncertain=TRUE)
obs <- single.snp.tests(cc, stratum, data=subject.support, snp.data=missing, score=TRUE)
imp <- single.snp.tests(cc, stratum, data=subject.support, snp.data=target, rules=rules, score=TRUE)
both <- pool(obs, imp)
both <- pool(obs, imp, score=TRUE)
sw.obs <- switch.alleles(obs, 1:3)

workflows.name: fst_calculation
workflows.intent: Calculate Wright's Fst coefficient to measure population differentiation across strata.
workflows.stages: 1. Calculate pairwise or overall Fst using Fst ;; 2. Compute weighted mean of Fst values
workflows.code:
data(for.exercise)
f1 <- Fst(snps.10, subject.support$stratum, pairwise=TRUE)
weighted.mean(f1$Fst, f1$weight)
f2 <- Fst(snps.10, subject.support$stratum, pairwise=FALSE)
weighted.mean(f2$Fst, f2$weight)
